_comment: Expected interpretation of the 6 UNSEEN postings, written by Claude from the captured posting text and the mode's documented policy (recipe v0.4 rules), BEFORE `triage.mjs run` was executed on them. Claude-reviewed, NOT human-validated. Claude wrote both these expectations and the rules, so agreement is weaker evidence than an independent reviewer's would be.

basis.G3: “If access to export-controlled technology or source code is required for performance of job duties, it is within Employer's discretion whether to apply for a U.S. government license … and Employer may decline to proceed with an applicant on this basis alone.” — export-control wording → a person (policy), not a refusal.
basis.G4: “8+ years of experience working on related systems preferred” — explicitly preferred; no required years.
basis.G6: “Strong software engineering skills in Java, Scala, C++, Go, Python …” under “What we look for” (a qualifications list) + distributed-systems responsibilities.
basis.note: “What we look for” is not in the rules' heading vocabulary; by source meaning it is the qualifications section.

basis.G4: “5+ years of software engineering experience, including substantial time working on large‑scale distributed systems or infrastructure.” — a general minimum (with a scoped clause); full-time 50–54 months < 60; with the 6-month co-op up to 60; silent on co-ops → review (Aditya's E14 rule). A section-unclear review would also be acceptable at gate level.
basis.G6: “proficient in one or more systems programming languages (e.g., C++, Rust, Go, Java, Scala)” + distributed systems / Kubernetes in the qualifications.

basis.G2: listed in the fresh feed; page check 'expired / insufficient content'; probe HTTP 403 'Just a moment...' 272 chars — a blocked page, not closure.
basis.G4: No years stated anywhere in the posting.
basis.G6: “Proficiency in software development languages such as Java, Python and C++” (What we’re looking for) + Kubernetes, AWS, distributed applications.

basis.G4: “10+ years of software engineering experience building and operating production systems …” — above everything the candidate has worked (≤ 60 months).
basis.G6: “Strong proficiency in Python and experience with at least one of: Java, Node.js, and/or Javascript” (required; Java is named) + distributed systems, event-driven, AWS.

basis.G3: “authorization and clearing flows with major global card networks” is CARD authorization, not work authorization.
basis.G4: “plus two (2) years of experience in Software Development” is general and met (50–54 ≥ 24), but “Must also have two (2) years of experience in each of the following … Java, Ruby, Scala, or Python …” and one (1) year in payments/ISO 8583/Cloud are scoped → unknown without scoped inputs.
basis.G6: Java is named in a required list, but by the rules' defined term groups there is no distributed-systems, messaging, or named cloud-infrastructure term (only “Cloud.” and API/REST). Rule-literal expectation; a person would likely call this backend work.

basis.G4: “Bachelor’s … plus five (5) years of post-bachelor’s progressive software development work experience. In the alternative, the employer is willing to accept a Master’s Degree … plus three (3) years of software development work experience.” — two branches across two sentences: a person decides (the MS is expected 2027-01, not held at capture). Also scoped “three (3) years … in each of the following”.
basis.G6: “Go, Ruby, or Java programming languages” (required) + “Designing fault-tolerant systems using data sharding and replication”.
